verdict.rationale: Semgrep Code is documented as a SAST tool (semgrep-docs-60) whose taint-tracking rules are built to catch injection bugs such as XSS (semgrep-docs-41, semgrep-docs-58). It runs locally via `semgrep scan` with no login required (semgrep-docs-27, semgrep-docs-34), and it offers cross-file analysis (semgrep-docs-2). Community users confirm they rely on it for security rules and curated per-language rulesets (semgrep-comm-1, semgrep-comm-7), though one hands-on test shows a simple exec pattern was evaded by aliasing (semgrep-comm-10). Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration that injection/XSS findings are detected out of the box, explicit documentation of prebuilt injection/XSS rulesets, and evidence that detection is robust to aliasing-style evasion.
